summary: Round 4. Verified the delta rather than taking it: git diff f4aa33a7b3e696b8a7663a67ae8cc7e62ad943ce (the staged_tree recorded with my round-3 pass) against git write-tree is exactly one added line, baselines/review.txt:36. No source, test, ADR or backlog byte moved. R3d is discharged: sequencer/build/reports/pitest/mutations.xml now parses, 99 KILLED + 10 TIMED_OUT + 9 SURVIVED + 1 NO_COVERAGE = 109/119 = 91.6%, matching the reported re-run and my round-3 hand count. I REPRODUCED THE ARGUMENT'S MEASUREMENT rather than accepting it: in an issued tree, 300 seeds x 120 rounds x 3 pods under unreachable-only 0.05 gives 0 violations on the staged bytes; reverting checkLink's `continuedAt() > epoch` plus the burned-gap loop to the pre-fix `continuedAt() != epoch` while keeping the production fix gives 287 violating seeds and {link=63081} -- 63,081 exactly, the number claimed, and 0 I2; and reverting the two production hunks while keeping the relaxed checkLink gives {I2=38}, so the checker half alone fixes no I2. Both halves of the cannot-ship-apart claim hold as stated. The two cap-forced splits are real: Invariants.java was 495 lines at HEAD (270 + CrossEpochInvariants 274 now), LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest 385 + LocalSequencerSealRaceTest 189 = 574. What does NOT hold is the entry's account of its own rounds, which is the one thing this line exists to record -- see M4.47-R4a. One major, in the added line, no code change required to fix it.

findings.finding: "⚠️ EVERY ROUND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN CODE, none in prose" is false in both halves, and .harness/review is the witness. (a) ONLY ROUND 1 PRODUCED A CHANGES-REQUESTED VERDICT. Round 2 (cf0286e7b8e7) is `pass` from reviewer (2 minors) and `pass` from test-reviewer (5 minors); round 3 (28ac1467c7f9) is `pass` from both (4 and 2 minors). The commit was landable at round 2, and rounds 3 and 4 follow from electing to act on minors plus a gate-state correction -- the disposition review.md's `minors-land` calls permitted and usually wrong. The entry's own next sentence concedes it ("Round 3: clean on both roles") and so contradicts the claim two clauses later. (b) "none in prose" is false of round 1: M4.47-R1c was ChainReplay.java:347-354, a javadoc caveat still asserting the empty-origin case was unhandled after the method had been changed to handle it -- "a comment stating the negation of its own method" -- fixed in round 2 alongside R1a and R1b. This file's own vocabulary two entries above classifies exactly that as prose: M4.10c's round 6 is labelled "PROSE ONLY" for "three production comments stating a REASON this commit made false". (c) The entry never says what round 4 is, so a reader gets review_rounds.py counting four rounds against prose accounting for three -- where the M4.10d entry describes the round it is being reviewed in ("Round 6 reviews that correction ... no production change"). Everything else in the line I re-measured and it is accurate to the digit.
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is append-only and is the artifact consulted when someone asks whether this project's round budget is being respected or gamed. A maintainer or agent auditing it reads that M4.47 needed four rounds because every one of them found a real code defect, concludes the cap is binding correctly, and cites M4.47 as the example of a task where extra rounds paid. The truth on record in .harness is one changes-requested round followed by three passes -- the same shape M4.13f's entry confesses in as many words ("ROUND 2 WAS A CLEAN PASS FROM BOTH ROLES, minors only, and the commit was landable there"). The two entries then say opposite things about the same practice, in the same file, and the false one is the newer. That is this project's named recurring failure -- one copy of a fact corrected and another left asserting the opposite, which backlog-done.md:115 records for M4.0 and this file records twice more -- landing permanently in the record whose entire purpose is to be honest about round counts. Remedy is one clause, not a rewrite and not a code change: replace "EVERY ROUND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN CODE, none in prose" with what the harness says -- round 1 changes-requested on a blocking production defect plus one stale javadoc, rounds 2 and 3 pass from both roles with minors only, round 4 reviewing this line.
